Q.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four factors courts weigh in a fair use analysis?
c: Purpose and character of the use
Q.e: The four factors are purpose/character, nature of the work, amount used, and effect on the market. Popularity isn't one.

Q.q: A student finds an image licensed CC BY-NC. What may the student do with it?
c: Use it anywhere with no credit
Use it with attribution for noncommercial purposes
Sell it on a T-shirt with attribution
Nothing; CC images can't be reused
Q.e: BY = give attribution. NC = noncommercial only.

Q.q: Which federal law protects the privacy of student education records?
Q.e: FERPA covers education records. COPPA covers online data from kids under 13; CIPA requires internet filtering for E-rate schools.

Q.q: An email claims to be from the district IT office and asks students to 'verify' their passwords at a link. This is an example of:
Q.e: Phishing uses a fake trusted sender to trick people into revealing credentials.

Q.q: Which file format uses LOSSLESS compression?
Q.e: PNG (also GIF, FLAC, ZIP) is lossless. JPEG, MP3 and most video codecs are lossy.

Q.q: Which type of memory is volatile and loses its contents when power is off?
Q.e: RAM is volatile working memory. ROM, SSDs and flash keep data without power.

Q.q: A teacher wants a quick check of whether each student understood today's loop lesson before tomorrow. Best choice?
c: An exit ticket with one tracing problem
Q.e: Exit tickets are fast formative assessment that inform the next day's instruction.

Q.q: Which is the BEST first step when judging whether a website is a credible source?
c: Check how attractive the design is
Check the author's credentials and publication date
See if it appears first in search results
Q.e: Authority and currency are core credibility checks. Search rank and design say nothing about accuracy.

Q.q: A district document that defines how students may and may not use school computers and networks is called a(n):
Q.e: An AUP sets rules for using school technology, including consequences for misuse.

Q.q: Everything a student posts, likes and shares online that can later be found is their:
Q.e: Digital footprint is a core digital citizenship concept.

Q.q: Which strategy best supports English language learners in a CS class?
c: Avoid diagrams so they focus on text
Pair vocabulary with visuals and examples, and allow partner talk
Grade spelling in code comments heavily
Q.e: Visuals, modeling, and structured peer talk are standard sheltered-instruction supports.

Q.q: A program compiles and runs but prints the wrong average because the loop skips the last element. What kind of error is this?
Q.e: It runs without crashing but gives the wrong result: a logic error (here, off-by-one).

Q.q: A program crashes when it divides by a user-entered value of 0. What kind of error is this?
Q.e: The code compiles, then fails while executing: a runtime error (ArithmeticException in Java).

Q.q: Valid input is an integer from 1 to 100. Which set of test values best performs boundary testing?
Q.e: Test just inside and just outside each boundary: 0, 1, 100, 101.

Q.q: Testing a function only by comparing outputs to the specification, without looking at the code, is:
Q.e: Black-box = based on specs/inputs/outputs. White-box = based on the internal code paths.

Q.q: Which development model delivers working software in short, repeated iterations with frequent customer feedback?
Q.e: Agile (e.g., Scrum sprints) is iterative and incremental. Waterfall runs phases once in sequence.

Q.q: In the software development life cycle, what normally comes FIRST?
Q.e: SDLC: requirements/analysis → design → implementation → testing → deployment → maintenance.

Q.q: About how many comparisons does binary search need, worst case, on a sorted list of 1,000 items?
Q.e: Binary search is O(log n). log₂(1000) ≈ 10.

Q.q: What is the Big-O time of this code?
Q.e: Two nested loops that each run n times → n × n = O(n²).

Q.q: Which sorting algorithm uses divide-and-conquer and runs in O(n log n) in every case?
Q.e: Merge sort splits, sorts halves recursively, and merges: O(n log n) best, average, and worst.

Q.q: After ONE pass of selection sort (ascending), what is [5, 2, 9, 1]?
Q.e: Selection sort finds the minimum (1) and swaps it into index 0: [1, 2, 9, 5].

Q.q: After ONE pass of bubble sort (ascending), what is [5, 2, 9, 1]?
Q.e: Swap 5/2 → [2,5,9,1]; 5/9 stays; swap 9/1 → [2,5,1,9]. The largest bubbles to the end.

Q.q: Which data structure is best for an 'Undo' feature?
Q.e: Undo reverses the most recent action first: last in, first out = stack.

Q.q: A stack: push 1, push 2, pop, push 3, pop. What did the SECOND pop return?
Q.e: After push 1, push 2, pop (→2), push 3, the top is 3, so the second pop returns 3.

Q.q: Breadth-first search of a graph typically uses which structure to track nodes to visit?
Q.e: BFS uses a FIFO queue. DFS uses a stack (or recursion).

Q.q: In a UML class diagram, what does a minus sign (−) before an attribute mean?
Q.e: + public, − private, # protected; underlined = static.

Q.q: Breaking a large problem into smaller subproblems that are each solved separately is called:
Q.e: Decomposition (top-down design / stepwise refinement). Abstraction hides unneeded detail.

Q.q: Insertion sort's BEST case occurs when the input is already sorted. Its best-case time is:
Q.e: Each element is compared once and never shifted: O(n).

Q.q: Average-case lookup time for a key in a well-designed hash table is:
Q.e: Hashing jumps straight to the bucket: O(1) on average (O(n) worst case with many collisions).

Q.q: A recursive method has no base case. When run, the most likely result is:
Q.e: Each call adds a stack frame until the call stack runs out.

Q.q: In pair programming, the person typing the code is the ____ and the person reviewing and guiding is the ____.
Q.e: Driver types; navigator reviews and thinks ahead. Partners swap roles often.

Q.q: Testing that verifies separately built modules work correctly TOGETHER is:
Q.e: Unit tests check one piece alone; integration tests check how pieces interact.

Q.q: What is the main purpose of a version control system like Git?
c: Track changes and let a team merge and roll back work
Q.e: Version control records history, supports branching/merging, and allows reverting.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: Integer division 17 / 5 = 3, and 17 % 5 = 2. 3 + 2 = 5.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: The cast applies to 7 first, so it's 7.0 / 2 = 3.5. (double)(7 / 2) would give 3.0.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: Indexes 2, 3, 4 (end is exclusive): M P U.

Q.q: How many times does the loop body run?
Q.e: i takes 0, 3, 6, 9, then 12 fails the test. Four iterations.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: length is 5, so a[3] = 16.

Q.q: What does f(5) return?
What does mystery(482) return?
Q.e: It sums the digits: 2 + 8 + 4 = 14.

Q.q: Which expression is equivalent to !(a && b)?
Q.e: De Morgan's law: NOT (A AND B) = (NOT A) OR (NOT B).

Q.q: What happens when x is 0?
c: Condition is false; nothing prints, no exception
Q.e: Short-circuit: x != 0 is false, so && never evaluates 10 / x.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: == compares references (two different objects). equals compares contents.

Q.q: What is printed?
Q.e: Polymorphism: the overridden method of the actual object type (Dog) runs at runtime.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: Java passes a copy of a primitive. Changing n doesn't change x.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: The reference is copied, but both point to the same array, so the change is visible.

Q.q: Making fields private and exposing them through getter and setter methods demonstrates:
Q.e: Encapsulation hides internal data and controls access.

Q.q: Two methods in the same class share a name but have different parameter lists. This is:
Q.e: Overloading = same name, different parameters (compile-time). Overriding = subclass redefines a superclass method.

Q.q: A class variable declared static is:
c: Shared by all objects of the class
Q.e: One static variable belongs to the class itself and is shared by every instance.

Q.q: What is the final value of n?
Q.e: 1 → 3 → 9 → 27 → 81 → 243. 81 < 100, so it multiplies once more.

Q.q: What is count after this runs?
Q.e: Inner loop runs 1, then 2, then 3 times: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

Q.q: What does this Python code print?
Q.e: Slices start at index 1 and stop before index 4.

Q.q: In Python, what is 7 // 2 + 2 ** 3?
Q.e: // is floor division (3). ** is exponent (8). 3 + 8 = 11.

Q.q: Given int[][] g = new int[3][4]; what are g.length and g[0].length?
Q.e: g.length = number of rows (3). g[0].length = columns in row 0 (4).

Q.q: Which expression gives a random integer from 1 to 6 inclusive?
Q.e: Math.random() is in [0, 1). × 6 → [0, 6); cast → 0–5; + 1 → 1–6. The last option casts first and always yields 1.

Q.q: In a try / catch / finally block, when does the finally block run?
c: Only if an exception is thrown
Only if no exception is thrown
Every time, whether or not an exception occurs
Q.e: finally always runs (cleanup like closing files).

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: 'A' is 65. 65 + 2 = 67, cast to char = 'C'.

Q.q: Which statement about an abstract class in Java is TRUE?
c: It can be instantiated with new
It cannot be instantiated, but it can have constructors and concrete methods
It can only contain abstract methods
Q.e: Abstract classes can't be created directly but can hold fields, constructors, and implemented methods.

Q.q: Which correctly describes Java versus Python execution?
c: Both compile straight to machine code
Java compiles to bytecode run by the JVM; Python is typically interpreted
Java is purely interpreted line by line
Q.e: javac → bytecode → JVM. CPython interprets (via its own bytecode) at runtime.

Q.q: What is printed? (Java)
Q.e: Java's % keeps the sign of the dividend: -7 = 3 × (-2) + (-1). (Python would print 2.)

Q.q: What is the value of this Boolean expression?
Q.e: (true) && false = false.

Q.q: Which correctly describes a constructor?
c: It has the same name as the class and no return type
It can only be called once per program
Q.e: Constructors share the class name, have no return type, and run when new creates an object.

Q.q: What is binary 101101 in decimal?
What is hexadecimal 2F in decimal?
What is the 8-bit two's complement representation of −1?
XOR outputs 1 when:
Q.e: XOR = exclusive or: true when inputs differ. 1 XOR 1 = 0.

Q.q: Which gate is 'universal,' meaning any logic circuit can be built from it alone?
Q.e: NAND (and NOR) are universal gates.
Inclusion-exclusion: 12 + 9 − 4 = 17.

Q.q: How many ways can 2 students be chosen from 5 for a team (order doesn't matter)?
In digital forensics, why is a hash (e.g., SHA-256) taken of a drive image?
c: To prove the copy is identical and unaltered
Q.e: Matching hashes before and after show the evidence wasn't changed. Chain of custody documents who handled it.

Q.q: A device that lets an investigator read a drive without changing any data on it is a:
Q.e: A write blocker allows read-only access to preserve evidence.

Q.q: A robot reads a distance sensor, the program decides, and a motor turns. The motor is the:
Q.e: Sense (sensor) → think (controller) → act (actuator).

Q.q: A robot continually adjusts its motor speed based on how far it is from a line it follows. This is:
Q.e: Using sensor feedback to correct output is closed-loop control (PID is a common example).

Q.q: The core loop of most video games repeats which steps each frame?
Q.e: Game loop: handle input → update game state (physics, collisions) → draw the frame.

Q.q: Which protocol translates a domain name like tea.texas.gov into an IP address?
Q.e: DNS resolves names to IP addresses. DHCP assigns IP addresses to devices.

Q.q: Which transport protocol guarantees ordered, reliable delivery?
Q.e: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable. UDP is faster but connectionless (streaming, games).

Q.q: What is decimal 255 in hexadecimal?
Q.e: 255 = 15 × 16 + 15 = FF. It is also the max value of one unsigned byte.

Q.q: In propositional logic, p → q is FALSE only when:
c: p is false and q is true
p is true and q is false
Q.e: An implication fails only when a true premise leads to a false conclusion.
